column1: # What each SPDX licence's own canonical text is expected to be identified as, where that is not
# simply "itself, and nothing else". tools/gate.py scans every text in data/spdx-texts.json.gz and
# compares against this file; anything unlisted must report exactly its own ID.
# This is the regression baseline for the corpus. A change to a pattern that alters what some
# licence text classifies as cannot land without a line here changing too, which is what makes it
# visible in review rather than a number in a test summary.
# Format: <licence whose text is scanned><TAB><IDs reported, comma separated, or "-" for none><TAB><why>

The Netrek variant differs from HPND only in wording the pattern treats as variable, so the more general pattern matches at least as much of it and wins on priority. Its own pattern is in the corpus and can still match real files that differ; reporting HPND here is the pre-existing behaviour, not a regression.
